title: Integer median on the unit cube: it minimizes the L¹ deviation and is bounded by twice the L¹ norm
statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). If u : ℝⁿ → ℝ takes only integer values (u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y) and is integrable on Q₁, then there is β ∈ ℤ with ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| for every c ∈ ℝ and |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∃ β : ℤ, (∀ c : ℝ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - c|) ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y|
